home.heroTitle: One piece, one original, one trace of the hand.
home.heroSub: A hundred ceramic pieces from Anna Ciok's small studio: mugs, small, medium and large vases, small dishes, large plates, large bowls and wavy-rim bowls. Each piece is hand-painted and glazed separately, so you choose the exact one shown in the photo.
home.colLead: Browse it like a gallery, mark the pieces you love, and head to checkout when your selection feels right.

mug.desc: Mugs for everyday coffee and tea. Palms, lemons, shells and cacti painted in glaze on pale clay.

vase.desc: Round-bellied vases for a single branch, a few tulips or a market bunch. Each one has its own rhythm of stripes and drawings.

midvase.desc: Medium vases with a clear character — somewhere between the small and the large format.

bigvase.desc: Large forms with a strong presence: palms, shells, cacti, a lobster and small folk scenes on warm white.

dish.desc: Small dishes for jewellery, olive oil, salt or the little things that gather by the bed. Small, but full of character.

medplate.desc: Medium plates, each hand-painted separately. For snacking, serving or displaying — ⌀ 18 cm.

plate.desc: Large plates for serving, collecting or hanging on the wall. A donkey, palms, eyes, shells and painted rims.

largebowl.desc: Generous bowls for fruit, salads and the things that like to live on the table. Inside: cobalt gardens, palms and leaves.

wavybowl.desc: Wavy-rim bowls for breakfast, snacks and small everyday rituals. Each one waves a little differently.

home.storyImageAlt: Anna Ciok in her ceramics studio
home.editorialImageAlt: Hand-painted Anna Ciok ceramics in sunlight
home.storyP1: I’m Anna. I paint canvases and ceramics, and both worlds meet in the same studio. I treat a mug, plate or vase like a small functional painting: something you can hold, place on the table and use without waiting for a special occasion.
home.storyP2: I work alone and slowly, one piece after another. The hand leaves its trace in the brush line, in an uneven palm and in a stripe that does not pretend to be perfect. That is where each piece gets its character.
home.storyP3: The June drop is one hundred and three pieces made this spring. When one finds its home, it leaves the shop for good.
home.craft1P: In the gallery, click the pieces that pull you in. Every selected thumbnail lands in the bar at the bottom of the screen, so it is easy to come back to your choice.
home.craft2P: In the cart, review your pieces, choose a parcel locker or courier delivery, and complete the order. Payment is handled by Stripe: card or Przelewy24.
home.craft3P: I wrap each piece by hand and ship within 1–3 business days. Since there is only one of each, your purchase removes it from the shop — no one buys the same one.
home.ctP: Want to see a piece or order something for a special occasion? Write to me — the fastest way to reach me is by email or on Instagram.

studio.lead: A small ceramics studio in Tenerife. Here I paint, glaze and refine every piece myself, one by one. This June drop travelled with me to Poland for the summer.
studio.workspaceImageAlt: Anna Ciok's ceramics studio in Tenerife
studio.storyP1: I’m Anna. I am a painter and ceramicist. I still paint canvases, but for the past few years ceramics has drawn me in more and more. I love that a painting can step off the wall, land in your hand and become part of an ordinary day.
studio.storyP2: I came to ceramics slowly: first a course, then a shelf in someone else’s studio, and finally my own small place with a glazing table, brushes and a kiln. It is calm, physical work, and it refuses to be rushed.
studio.storyP3: I paint by hand, without transfers or stencils. That is why a line sometimes wanders, a palm leans a little, and two similar motifs are never truly the same. For me, that is where the object starts to feel alive.
studio.fact1D: One room, a glazing table, brushes and a kiln.
studio.fact2D: After painting and glazing, each piece goes into the kiln, where the firing sets the colour and turns the surface into a glassy, functional layer.
studio.fact3D: Mugs, small, medium and large vases, small dishes, medium plates, large plates, large bowls and wavy-rim bowls. Every piece is one of a kind.
studio.fact4D: I pack every parcel by hand and ship across Poland.
studio.procH: From the first layer to a finished piece.
studio.p1P: I start by looking over each piece, planning the motif and choosing the glaze colours. Then comes quiet work, layer by layer.
studio.p2P: On the pale ceramic surface I apply glaze and paint the motif with a brush: palms, lemons, shells, cacti, stripes. This is when each piece finds its own rhythm.
studio.p3P: The firing sets the glaze and colour. I look the finished piece over carefully, sign the base and place it on the shelf, where it waits for its home.
studio.ctaP: When a piece finds its home, it leaves the shop for good. Take a look at what’s waiting in the June drop.

shipping.lead: How I pack, how long the parcel takes, and what to do if a piece arrives damaged. Everything before you click “buy”.
shipping.s1P: I ship by InPost Parcel Locker (from 20 zł) or courier (30 zł) across all of Poland. Shipping costs the same regardless of how many pieces you order — if you buy several, they travel together in one parcel.
shipping.s1Li1: InPost Parcel Locker, all of Poland — from 20 zł
shipping.s1Li1b: InPost courier, all of Poland — 30 zł
shipping.s1Li3: International shipping — write to me and I’ll arrange it individually
shipping.s2P: The June-drop pieces are finished and already waiting in Poland, so there’s no production time. I send the parcel within 1–3 business days of the payment clearing, and the courier usually delivers the next day.
shipping.s2Note: I pack everything myself, between studio work and the next firings. If you need a specific date, write to me and I’ll check what is possible.
shipping.s3P: The ceramics travel wrapped by hand — film, cardboard and plenty of padding so nothing moves. I label the box as fragile. I try to limit plastic wherever I can, without risking the piece.
shipping.s4P: Live in Warsaw or passing through? You can collect your order in person — then shipping is free. We arrange the pickup by email for a specific day and time; this is not a fixed-hours pickup point.
shipping.s5P: As a consumer you have the right to withdraw from the purchase within 14 days of receiving the parcel, with no reason needed. You can start your return on the returns page — just your order number. You can also write to hej@ciok.art.
shipping.s5Li1: The piece should come back undamaged, ideally in its original packaging
shipping.s5Li2: The cost of return shipping is on the buyer
shipping.s5Li3: I refund within 14 days of receiving the piece back
shipping.s6P: Ceramics can be fragile, and couriers vary. If a parcel arrives broken, please photograph the contents and the packaging and send the photos to me the same day. I’ll replace the piece with another from the drop or refund the full amount including shipping — your choice.

terms.lead: The rules for buying at Anna Ciok Ceramics. Written plainly, without the legal fog — so you can actually read them.
terms.s1P1: The Anna Ciok Ceramics online shop is run by the ceramics studio of Anna Ciok, based in Warsaw. You can contact the seller at <link>hej@ciok.art</link>.
terms.s1P2: The items for sale are hand-painted ceramic pieces. Each piece is the only copy — once sold it disappears from the offer and is not remade.
terms.s2P: You place an order by adding selected pieces to the cart and confirming the purchase. The sale contract is concluded the moment the order is confirmed and the payment clears.
terms.s2Li1: Because each piece is unique, any given piece can be sold only once
terms.s2Li2: If for reasons beyond my control I cannot fulfil an order, I inform you immediately and refund the full amount
terms.s3P: All prices are given in Polish złoty (PLN) and are gross prices. The shipping cost shown in the cart before you confirm is added to the order total. Payment is handled by a secure external payment provider, Stripe.
terms.s4P: I send orders within 1–3 business days of the payment clearing. Details of costs, timing and pickup are described on the <link>Shipping & returns</link> page.
terms.s5P: A consumer has the right to withdraw from the purchase within 14 days of receiving the piece, without giving a reason. The statement can simply be sent by email. The returned piece should be undamaged; the buyer covers the return shipping, and the refund is made within 14 days.
terms.s6P: If a piece arrives damaged or not as described, you can file a complaint by email, attaching photos. I review it within 14 days and — depending on your choice — replace the piece or refund the full amount including shipping.
terms.s7P: Matters not covered by these terms are governed by Polish law, including the Consumer Rights Act and the Civil Code. Any changes to the terms do not affect orders placed before they take effect.

privacy.lead: What data I collect, what for, and for how long. Short, because there isn’t much data — this is a small studio, not a corporation.
privacy.s1P: The controller of your data is the ceramics studio of Anna Ciok, based in Warsaw. For matters relating to personal data, write to <link>hej@ciok.art</link>.
privacy.s2Li1: Data needed to fulfil an order — name, shipping address, email and phone number
privacy.s2Li2: The content of any message you send me by email
privacy.s2Li4: Payment data needed to complete your order — processed directly by <link>Stripe</link>; your full payment details never reach my servers
privacy.s2Li3: Basic technical browser data needed for the site and cart to work
privacy.s2P: I don’t collect data I don’t need, and I don’t sell it to anyone.
privacy.s3P: I process data to fulfil an order, reply to a message, handle payment and meet tax obligations. Payments are handled by <link>Stripe</link> as an external provider — I never see or store your full card details. The basis is performance of the contract and, for accounting, a legal obligation.
privacy.s4P: I keep order data for as long as tax regulations require. I delete email correspondence once the matter is settled, unless further correspondence requires keeping it.
privacy.s5P: The site uses essential cookies and browser storage to remember the contents of your cart. If you consent, analytics and marketing tools may also run. During checkout, <link>Stripe</link> sets its own cookies needed to process payment securely and prevent fraud.
privacy.s6P: You have the right to access your data, correct it, delete it and restrict its processing. Just write to me — I’ll reply as fast as I can.

A black donkey with a white harness pattern and a terracotta wavy border with white lines. The motif stands quietly in profile, and the edge leads the rhythm around.
A brown palm with light veining, blue fruits and a blue frill with white dots. The holiday motif spreads wide across the light bottom of the plate.
A terracotta palm with white lines, black fruits and a black wavy border with light strokes. The desert motif stands in the center, and the edge guides it with a soft rhythm.
A black donkey with a white garland on its side and a terracotta frill with white dots on the edge. The folk motif stands in the center of the plate, and the rim beats an even rhythm.
A black flower with a dotted center, round petals and herringbone leaves. The straight vertical of the stem arranges the motif calmly on the light plate.
A black palm with white lines, brown fruits and a brown frill with white dots. The leaves spread wide, and the edge leads a holiday rhythm around.
A black figure in a wide hat and a skirt in a light grid, surrounded by a terracotta frill with white lines. The folk motif stands vertically in the center of the plate.
A black figure in a wide hat and a striped jacket with checkered trousers. Terracotta strokes on the rim beat an even rhythm around the edge.
talerze-duze: Brown donkey with a white garland on its side and a black wave at the rim. The motif stands calmly in the center, while the striped edge leads a rhythm around.
Terracotta shell with white lines on a bright background of the plate. A black wavy border with light hatching leads a rhythm around the edge.
Terracotta shell in the center of the plate, crossed by light vertical lines. A black wavy rim leads a rhythm of short strokes around it.
Black cactus with light incised thorns and a terracotta wave at the edge. The desert motif stands in the middle of the plate, and the wavy border leads a rhythm around.
Blue flowers with light centers and thin lines of petals. The motif scatters across the wide plate in a calm, soft rhythm.
Blue lemon in the center and black bands on the wide rim. The rhythm of the border leads the eye to light incisions scattered on the fruit.
Blue leaf with light veins crosses the bright bottom of the plate. Lines run calmly along the shape, from the narrow stem to the rounded edge.
Blue wreath of leaves with white hatching and a white star in the center. Terracotta marks with light incisions on the rim beat an even rhythm around the plate.
Terracotta eye with radiating lines and blue rectangles on the rim. The motif spreads from the center, and the edge beats an even, light rhythm.
duze-michy: Blue flowers, leaves, and a shell are arranged within the light-colored bowl. A wavy blue band on the outside leads a calm rhythm around the form.
Black flowers on thin stems and terracotta herringbone leaves. The motif runs lightly along the interior and the wavy edge of the bowl.
Terracotta palms with fine linework and black fruits. The motif circles the interior, and the wavy rim adds movement.
Brown saguaro cacti and black diamonds with a terracotta dot. The desert motif runs around the light interior of the bowl.
A black garden in the center of the bowl: a dotted flower, herringbone leaves, and flexible stems. The motif spreads freely across the light interior and reaches up to the rounded rim.
Black palms with white veining and terracotta fruits on the light interior of the bowl. The motif sways across the interior, and a terracotta wavy line near the outer rim adds a soft rhythm.
miski-falowane: Black saguaro with small terracotta protrusions and round suns. A desert motif spreads across the wavy interior of the bowl.
Black shells around a terracotta starfish on the light bottom of the bowl. The wavy rim leads the sea motif around with a soft rhythm.
Black cacti with light incisions and terracotta ovals on a light background. The motif circles inside the bowl, following the wavy edge.
Black poppies with thin veins and terracotta chevron leaves. The motif circles the light interior, emphasizing the wavy edge of the bowl.
Blue cacti with white incisions and terracotta dots on the light interior of the bowl. The desert motif flows along the wavy rim in a light, irregular rhythm.
Blue palms with terracotta fruits on the light interior of the bowl. The motif flows around along the wavy rim.
Terracotta palms with light chevron hatching and black fruits on the light interior of the bowl. The motif flows around the wavy form, and a black wavy band on the outside echoes the rhythm.
Blue shells around a terracotta starfish on the light bottom of the bowl. A terracotta wavy band on the outside emphasizes the rim and leads the sea rhythm around the form.
Blue lemons with small white lines on the light interior. The fruity rhythm circles along the wavy rim and descends toward the center.
Black branches with round berries and chevron leaves. The motif spreads across the light interior, and the wavy rim leads it with a soft rhythm.
